title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming formatting and tool calls
author: Asha Patel
body:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions closer to parity with common upstream behavior (params, roles handling, stop token semantics, logprobs shape) and address several streaming stability and tool/function-calling edge-cases observed in production. This PR implements canonical parameter mapping, preserves role annotations across transformations, emits stop/logprobs in the OpenAI-compatible shape when requested, and stabilizes streaming framing and flush behavior so function/tool calls and structured JSON outputs are reliably delivered to clients.

What changed (summary):
- Parameter mapping: map OpenAI parameters (temperature, top_p, n, max_tokens, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias) to internal runtime knobs with documented fallbacks and validation. Added explicit handling for `n>1` response multiplexing.
- Roles: preserve `role` fields exactly as supplied in messages (user/system/assistant/custom) through tokenization and KV-cache indexing to avoid role-loss during merges/rollouts.
- stop/logprobs: implement OpenAI-shaped `choices[*].logprobs` and `usage` when `logprobs` or `stop` are provided; handle mixed string/array stop tokens and early termination semantics.
- Streaming stability: improved chunk framing with explicit event boundaries, backpressure-aware flush thresholds, and a deterministic finalization event when structured output or tool calls are completed.
- Tool/Function calling: ensure tool invocation metadata is streamed incrementally and that tool-result fragments are re-assembled deterministically at the client boundary; added guardrails for partial-tool responses and retries.
- Structured output formatting: added JSON-safe streaming helpers (chunk-level linting and incremental recovery) and schema-hint pass-through for client-side validation.
- Tests & docs: added e2e parity tests (unit/integration), updated OpenAI-compat docs and examples, and added benchmarks for streaming latency.

Implementation notes:
- Changes are split between the API compatibility layer and the runtime streaming paths. The compatibility layer now centralizes mapping/validation so SDKs and internal endpoints get consistent behavior. The runtime changes are conservative and include a small compatibility flag to toggle the new framing for backporting to older clusters.
- Performance: added microbenchmarks; streaming framing improvements slightly increase CPU per-chunk but reduce end-to-end tail latency on 95/99p due to fewer re-transmits and more deterministic flushes.

Testing and rollout:
- Added unit tests for parameter validation, roles preservation, stop token edge-cases, and logprobs formatting.
- Integration E2E harness validated responses against OpenAI fixtures for 1x and 3x tokens and for `n=1/2`.
- Canary rollout plan: enable on staging -> gated on synthetic e2e and 1-hour live canary traffic -> gradual rollout to prod with quick rollback flag.

Checklist:
- [x] API mapping implemented and validated
- [x] Roles preserved through runtime pipeline
- [x] stop/logprobs shape implemented and covered by tests
- [x] Streaming framing & flush improvements implemented and benchmarked
- [x] Tool/function streaming edge-cases tested
- [x] Docs updated

Notes for reviewers: pay particular attention to the stop token semantics (mixed arrays vs string) and the deterministic finalization event we introduced for structured outputs - this changes the exact sequence of streaming events but keeps compatibility with downstream SDKs by providing a single final sentinel. If we prefer, we can gate the sentinel behind a feature flag for a slower rollout.
commits: add: openai chat.completions param mapping and validation
fix: preserve message role tokens across KV-cache and merges
feat: openai-shaped stop/logprobs and usage reporting
perf(streaming): deterministic chunk framing and flush thresholds
fix(tool-calls): incremental tool-result reassembly and retry guard
test: add e2e compatibility tests and fixtures
review_comments: Evan Wright: Can you add a short note in the docs about how mixed-type stop tokens are interpreted? Some downstream SDKs expect array behavior.
Asha Patel: Added detailed section in docs/openai-compat/chat-completions.md and unit tests covering mixed-type stops.
Lena Gomez: Streaming E2E flaked once on integration (partial tool output). Please add a defensive reassembly test and increase flush timeout for slow networks.
Asha Patel: Added reassembly test and increased default flush threshold to 150ms on high-latency canaries; left flag to tune later.
Marco Silva: Approving - verified 1h canary and e2e fixtures. Two small nits about log messages and a missing lint rule which I left inline.
Asha Patel: Addressed nits and fixed lint failure.
ci_checks: integration-e2e: pass (rerun after flaky tool test)
release_notes: Adds OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for params, roles, stop/logprobs and improved streaming response formatting; fixes streaming stability and tool/function calling edge-cases. No breaking changes.
notes: Backported minimal runtime patch to stabilize streaming on 2.x clusters; kept a runtime feature flag for gradual rollout. Follow-up: instrument structured-output finalization event in Redwood Console for per-route SLOs.
